# `silk/schema/path`

<!-- Generated by silk doc-reference. Do not edit by hand. -->

Where in a value a schema problem is: the steps from the root value to the part that failed.

## When to use
Read a [`SchemaPath`](#SchemaPath) from a `silk.schema.issue.SchemaError` to say where a value failed, as
`settings.ports[2]` for a person with [`SchemaPath.text`](#SchemaPath.impl.text), or as the JSON Pointer
`/settings/ports/2` for a tool with [`SchemaPath.pointer`](#SchemaPath.impl.pointer).

## Details
A path keeps its steps, not text, so one error renders in every form. A field step holds both
the field's Silk name and its name on the wire, and a variant step names the variant a tagged
union chose, so `auth.Basic.user` says which variant `user` belongs to.

Import as `SchemaPath` with `import silk.schema.path { SchemaPath }`.

<a id="SchemaPath"></a>

## `SchemaPath`

```silk
pub struct SchemaPath
```

The path from the root value to the part a reader is reading, such as `settings.ports[2]`.

### When to use

A format's `SchemaReader` keeps one and returns it from `SchemaReader.path`. The derived
`read` operations push a segment before they read a part and pop it after, so when a read fails
the path still names the part that failed.

<a id="SchemaPath.impl.pointer"></a>

### Method `pointer`

```silk
pub effect fn pointer(self: &Self) -> String ! OutOfMemoryError ? &mut Allocator
```

Returns the path as a JSON Pointer (RFC 6901) into the input, such as `/auth/user` or
`/ports/2`. A variant step is left out, because the input has no member for it. The root value
is empty text.

#### Errors

- `OutOfMemoryError` if the `Allocator` cannot supply the text.
